overloadMerges.note: The docs render two syntax lines that differ only in whether the leading '*' is passed (selecting whether 'object' is an object-name string vs. a form variable reference). That's one semantic overload with an optional literal-symbol discriminator, not two independent overloads.

params.description: If present, object is a form object name (string); if omitted, object is a variable reference.

params.name: object
params.description: Form object name (if * is passed) or variable reference (if * is omitted), designating the target array-type list box.

params.name: hierarchical
params.description: True to display the list box in hierarchical mode; False for non-hierarchical (standard array) mode.

params.name: hierarchy
params.description: Array of pointers to the arrays used to construct the hierarchy. If omitted while switching to hierarchical mode: the first array is used by default if the list box was never hierarchical, or the last hierarchy is re-established if it was previously declared hierarchical; if the list box is already hierarchical, the command does nothing.

overloadMerges.semanticRole: Switches the designated array-type list box between hierarchical and non-hierarchical display mode, optionally designating which arrays define the hierarchy.

constraints: This command only functions with list boxes based on arrays; when used with a selection-based list box, it does nothing.
